mostWorthwhile.text: Making the protein brought the pieces together: RNA gave the order, amino acids formed the chain, and ATP helped power the work.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mitochondria was straightforward, but their folded inner membranes were shown without explaining what the folds do.

surprise.text: I was surprised that glucose was used up to make ATP, rather than staying attached to the membrane; the inset helped connect it with oxygen and the mitochondria.

arbitrary.text: The final pairing followed the named goal, but exactly how ATP helps the ribosome build a protein was not explained, so that connection felt partly like following a hint.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: connecting food, cell structures and protein building was interesting, though I would hope for more explanation of unfamiliar details.
